data.title: Spider-Man’s box-office reign could get tangled up by ‘Practical Magic 2’
data.description:
Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) is looking to take the top spot at the North American box office this weekend with “Practical Magic 2,” as the Warner Bros. (WBD) sequel opens against Sony Group’s (SONY) “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” which has led the domestic chart for six consecutive weekends.

Forecasts for the Sandra Bullock-Nicole Kidman sequel vary. Boxoffice Pro projects a $40 million-$50 million opening, while Variety expects $30 million-$40 million from about 4,000 North American theaters. The trade publication expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to take in $9 million to $11 million in its seventh weekend, while Universal’s (CMCSA) "The Odyssey" is projected at $6 million to $8 million.

The “Practical Magic” sequel is being released by Warner Bros. (WBD) at a time when the major-studio release calendar has been relatively light, giving the film a chance to capture demand after a record-setting summer for US theaters. Boxoffice Pro described it as the week’s destination movie by default amid the shortage of major studio releases.

For “Spider-Man,” the weekend could mark another milestone even as it loses the top spot. The Sony-Marvel film is closing in on the domestic box-office record held by “Star Wars: The Force Awakens,” which finished its run with about $936.7 million. Current tracking expects “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” to surpass that mark this weekend, ending the more than decade-long reign of “The Force Awakens.”

The weekend follows a record US summer box office of about $4.76 billion, underscoring the strong momentum heading into the fall release slate.

data.title: Pharming wins approval of Joenja for younger age group
data.description:
• The US FDA has approved Pharming Group's (PHAR) Joenja (leniolisib) for children between the ages of four and 11 with a kind of rare genetic immune system disorder.
  • The treatment was previously approved in 2023 for individuals 12 years and older with activated phosphoinositide 3-kinase delta syndrome (APDS).
  • Approval was based on safety and pharmacokinetic data from a single-arm, open-label study.
  • Individuals with APDS suffer from recurrent infections, especially in the sinuses, ears, and respiratory tract. They also develop enlarged lymph nodes, tonsils, and spleen.

data.title: Rent the Runway shares stumble as fewer subscribers, cash needs weigh
data.description:
Rent the Runway (RENT) is limping into the end of the week at an all-time low and five straight days of losses as another decline in active subscribers and a fresh share offering outweighed constructive Q2 results and a new CEO.

Shares were down by nearly 20% at midday.

Thanks to a subscription price increase and an increase in the volume of add-on bookings, total revenue for the quarter increased 20.8%, and rental revenue was up 21% year-over-year. 

This was overshadowed, however, by 3.8% fewer active subscribers in the second quarter, an outcome interim CFO David Loretta attributes to the stronger promotional activity last year and a higher rate of pause activity this year.

The company’s guidance also disappointed, as Q3 revenue guidance of $87M to $90M reflects flat to low single-digit growth compared to the same quarter last year. Full-year revenue growth was reaffirmed, and adjusted EBITDA margin is still expected to be between 4% and 7%.

Besides the loss in active subscribers and lackluster guidance, Rent the Runway (RENT) shares were also pinned down by plans for a $15M rights offering and a $10M term loan, underscoring the company’s need for cash.

data.title: Kroger lowers identical sales guide to 0.2%-0.8% while maintaining $5.10-$5.30 EPS outlook
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: The Kroger Co. (KR) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "This quarter reinforced my view that we are pointed in the right direction." (CEO & Director Gregory Foran) "Our identical sales without fuel grew 0.2% this quarter" and "adjusted earnings per diluted share was $1.09," while "sales were tracking well through the quarter until our final period when we absorbed the impact of the Cyclospora outbreak" that "cost us roughly 35 basis points of total company IDs without fuel." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • "E-commerce had a strong quarter" with "adjusted e-commerce sales grew 20%" and "retail media grew 24% during the quarter, our best since 2021, with media monetization up 88 basis points." (CEO & Director Foran) He also said "we delivered our second consecutive quarter of profitable e-commerce growth" and highlighted loyalty changes: "we expanded our loyalty program and rebranded Fuel Points as simply Points." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • "This quarter, we welcomed Emilee De Martino as our Chief People Officer" and "Nate Faust as Executive Vice President and Chief E-commerce Officer" and "Mark Ibbotson as Executive Vice President and Chief Store Operations Officer." (CEO & Director Foran) He also discussed M&A timing: "We continue to expect the transaction to close in 2027" regarding "our planned acquisition of Giant Eagle." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • "Sales were softer than we planned, and we still delivered the profit we committed to." (Executive VP & CFO David John Kennerley) "Our adjusted FIFO operating profit in the quarter was $1.1 billion" and "our FIFO gross margin rate... increased 13 basis points versus the second quarter of last year." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

Outlook

  • "We are lowering our full year identical sales without fuel guidance to a new range of 0.2% to 0.8% from our initial range of 1% to 2%." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley) He said the company is "maintaining our full year guidance for adjusted FIFO operating profit of $5 billion to $5.2 billion and adjusted net earnings per diluted share of $5.10 to $5.30." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • "In the opening weeks of the third quarter, we continue to see lingering impacts from Cyclospora." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley) He also flagged Q4 pressures: "The identical sales without fuel impact from the Inflation Reduction Act is projected to accelerate to approximately 150 basis points" and "we will begin to cycle the sales benefit from our new third-party delivery partnerships" plus "significant weather-related sales benefits from last year"; "we anticipate ID sales without fuel will be slightly better in Q3 than in Q4." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

Financial Results

  • "Adjusted EPS was $1.09, representing 5% growth versus last year." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley) He said "adjusted FIFO operating profit in the quarter was $1.1 billion" and "identical sales growth without fuel" was "0.2%." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Kennerley detailed sales headwinds: "the Inflation Reduction Act... was an approximately 140 basis point headwind"; "the ongoing shift from brand to generic prescriptions reduced sales by approximately 60 basis points"; "the impact from Cyclospora... was a 35 basis point headwind"; and "the lingering effect of egg deflation was another 30 basis point headwind"; "these headwinds represented a 265 basis point drag on identical sales without fuel." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • On costs and margins, Kennerley said FIFO gross margin improvement was "primarily driven by e-commerce profitability and media, pharmacy mix, tariff refunds and sourcing initiatives" but "partially offset by higher shrink, increased transportation costs and investments in customer value." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley) He added "we again delivered savings above our plan" and "fuel redemptions increased nearly 6% versus last year." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • On balance sheet and capital returns, Kennerley said "Kroger's net debt to adjusted EBITDA was 1.91" versus a "target ratio range of 2.3 to 2.5," and "through the first half of the year, we repurchased approximately $1.2 billion of shares under our existing $2 billion authorization." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

Q&A

  • Michael Lasser, UBS: Question on price investment and price gaps; CEO & Director Foran: "We're not providing exact figures on the investment" but "our pricing relative to some of our competitors... has actually improved" and "we've maintained that gap through Q2" versus "Rest of Market." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • Robert Ohmes, BofA: Question on inflation outlook; CEO & Director Foran: "I would expect that the pressure is actually going to mount"; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: "our range is within this 1% to 2.5% range for the balance of the year" and "I expect us to be below CPI." (CEO & Director Foran; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Edward Kelly, Wells Fargo: Question on simplifying pricing; CEO & Director Foran: "This is a multiyear program" and "we apply those savings to our shelf prices" while "you come up with a promotional mix that makes sense." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • John Heinbockel, Guggenheim: Question on perception vs. reality; CEO & Director Foran: "part of this is coming up with the right marketing package" and "well over half do not" understand the promotional package, based on "the research that we've done in 84.51°." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • Kelly Bania, BMO: Question on core comp and share; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: "that's roughly a 265 basis point headwind" and "we maintained the gap that we saw in Q1 in Q2" versus "Circana's Rest of Market." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Leah Jordan, Goldman Sachs: Question on fuel margin in guide; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: fuel profit "was basically... low single-digit profit growth" and the guide assumes "fuel margin softer than H1." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Simeon Gutman, Morgan Stanley: Question on profit protection vs. transformation; CEO & Director Foran: "I see even more opportunities than what I thought" and "I'm pretty comfortable that we'll do it in Q3 and Q4." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • Thomas Palmer, JPMorgan: Question on gross margin drivers and tariffs quantification; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: tariff refunds were "pretty modest" and "overall, it was a neutral impact to gross margin because we reinvested that money back." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Gregory Melich, Evercore: Question on traffic up/ticket down; CEO & Director Foran: "we did have traffic up slightly" and "ticket was down" as "the customer is pretty disciplined." (CEO & Director Foran)

  • Krisztina Katai, Deutsche Bank: Question on what’s working and diesel/freight; CEO & Director Foran: "if anything has a natural, organic, protein, health component to it... that's working extremely well"; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: "we have assumed that we will get some incremental headwinds from diesel and freight costs." (CEO & Director Foran; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Rupesh Parikh, Oppenheimer: Question on store growth vs. M&A; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley: "It's going to be a clear element of our strategy going forward, which is to open more stores" while M&A will be evaluated "extremely disciplined about capital allocation." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Scott Marks, Jefferies: Question on supplier price increases; CEO & Director Foran: "We've got a number of things in our toolkit" including Our Brands and "Smart Ways products... circa from about 130, we'll get that up to 1,000 over the next year and a bit." (CEO & Director Foran)

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst sentiment was slightly negative to neutral, with repeated probing on price investment quantification, comp deceleration mechanics, fuel/margin sustainability, and supplier pricing pressure (e.g., "how much did you invest in price" and "quantify... the tariff refund"). (Michael Lasser, UBS; Thomas Palmer, JPMorgan)

  • Management sentiment was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more defensive/controlled in Q&A, repeatedly emphasizing multiyear pacing and limited disclosure (e.g., "We're not providing exact figures" and "we're not going to quantify the number"). (CEO & Director Foran; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Versus Q1, the tone shifted toward more caution on sales: Q2 included "We are lowering our full year identical sales without fuel guidance" after Q1 said "we are reaffirming our full year guidance." (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley; previous-quarter remarks from Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Guidance language tightened in Q2: "lowering our full year identical sales without fuel guidance" to "0.2% to 0.8%" from "1% to 2%," while maintaining profit and EPS ranges. (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Business drivers shifted from Q1’s broad transformation framing to Q2’s event-driven headwinds and mitigation: Q2 highlighted "Cyclospora" impacts and Q4 pharmacy comparisons, while continuing to stress "savings fund value" and "profitable e-commerce growth." (CEO & Director Foran; Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Analyst focus moved from early-CEO strategy and timing (Q1 emphasis on "price investments" and cost opportunity sizing) to Q2’s reconciliation of weaker sales vs. profit durability, fuel margin assumptions, and tariff refund magnitude. (Q1/Q2 Q&A sequences across UBS, JPMorgan, Goldman)

Risks and Concerns

  • Sales risk centered on external and timing factors: "Cyclospora" lingering into Q3, and Q4 headwinds from "Inflation Reduction Act" acceleration plus cycling delivery and weather benefits. (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley)

  • Margin/cost risks included "higher shrink" ("mainly in fresh") and "increased transportation costs" tied to fuel and diesel, with mitigation framed as savings-funded value and ongoing productivity ("chasing every dollar we can save"). (Executive VP & CFO Kennerley; CEO & Director Foran)

Final Takeaway

Kroger’s management framed Q2 as proof it can protect earnings amid softer sales, citing $1.09 adjusted EPS and improved gross margin while cutting full-year identical sales without fuel guidance to 0.2%-0.8% due to Cyclospora, pharmacy-related headwinds, and tougher Q4 comparisons. Leadership emphasized e-commerce and retail media growth (20% and 24%, respectively), ongoing cost savings to fund value investments, and a stepped-up operating cadence supported by new executives, while maintaining full-year adjusted FIFO operating profit guidance of $5B-$5.2B and adjusted EPS guidance of $5.10-$5.30 ahead of an October investor update.

data.title: Palantir's push for AI sovereignty resonates with clients: DA Davidson
data.description:
Palantir's (PLTR) focus on the importance of AI sovereignty appears to be resonating with its clients, prompting D.A. Davidson to increase its price target on the stock to $250 from $200 and reiterate its Buy rating.

"Palantir's push into data sovereignty is resonating with customers," said D.A. Davidson analyst Gil Luria in an investor note. "Customers are getting savvier about what AI model they need and how to work with a range of models, and Palantir is capitalizing on that trend."

"Trust means Palantir is naturally positioned to become the control plane, orchestration layer and harness provider for a wide range of customers," he added. "Palantir is creating those layers for customers and solving the problem of choosing models and managing token costs."

On Thursday, Palantir hosted its eleventh annual AIPCon in Miami. The event featured presenters from Acrisure, Cisco (CSCO), Eaton (ETN), Federal Aviation Administration, Hexion, L3Harris (LHX), Nvidia (NVDA), Ondas Sentinel, USA TODAY (TDAY), Zeta Global (ZETA) and others.

"The NVIDIA announcement really drove home the point about trust," Luria added. "Palantir built a supply management system for NVIDIA leveraging Nemotron, which appears to address one of the most important challenges for the most important company in the world."

data.title: Home sellers outnumber buyers by record margin as mortgage rates hit 15-month high
data.description:
The U.S. housing market is facing a growing imbalance between sellers and buyers, with the gap reaching a record high as elevated mortgage rates continue to weigh on housing demand.

Home sellers outnumbered buyers by 57.9% in August, the largest gap on record, according to Redfin data shown in a chart shared by Liz Ann Sonders. The surplus widened from about 10% in early 2024 to more than 40% later in 2025 before reaching the latest record.

Mortgage rates have climbed to a 15-month high, with 30-year fixed-rate mortgages averaging 6.76% as of Sept. 10, up from 6.71% a week earlier and 6.35% a year ago, according to the Weekly Mortgage Applications Survey. The average 15-year fixed rate rose to 6.09%, from 6.04% last week and 5.50% a year ago.

The rise in borrowing costs comes as markets focus on the Federal Open Market Committee's upcoming meeting, with the path of interest rates remaining a key factor for the housing market.

data.title: Hooker Furnishings outlines Margaritaville rollout with about 100 in-store galleries and 10 freestanding stores
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Hooker Furnishings Corporation (HOFT) Q2 fiscal 2027

Management View

  • “Despite continued weaknesses in the housing market, soft retail demand for furniture and home furnishings, and persistent macroeconomic challenges, we delivered a consolidated net income of $1.7 million, marking our third consecutive profitable quarter.” (CFO Earl Armstrong)

  • “We've included a table in our earnings release showing the impacts of this quarter's tariff recoveries by operating segment and for the total company.” (CFO Armstrong) “Prior to the U.S. Supreme Court's February 2026 decision invalidating IEEPA tariffs, we incurred an estimated $10.3 million of cumulative pre-tax costs related to tariffs in our fiscal year 2026 results.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • “We are encouraged to report $1.7 million in consolidated net income for the quarter, marking our third consecutive quarter of profitability.” (CEO Jeremy Hoff) “The improvement reflects the benefit of tariff recoveries received during the quarter, as well as the sustained impact of the $17.5 million in annualized fixed cost reductions implemented across continuing operations in the prior year.” (CEO Hoff)

  • “Seasonally softer summer shipments to brick-and-mortar retailers resulted in a greater mix of e-commerce sales along with targeted promotional activity designed to support consumer engagement.” (CEO Hoff) “The combination of channel mix and elevated promotional activity pressured margins during the quarter.” (CEO Hoff)

Outlook

  • “Looking to the second half of fiscal '27, consumer spending remains selective.” (CEO Jeremy Hoff) “Housing turnover and big-ticket discretionary demand remain weak, and we do not expect meaningful near-term improvement in market conditions.” (CEO Hoff)

  • “We expect promotional activity to normalize during the second half of the fiscal year, much like we saw in July, the last month of our fiscal second quarter.” (CEO Hoff) “We believe that positive momentum will continue into the second half of the fiscal year.” (CEO Hoff)

  • “We now have commitments for approximately 100 in-store galleries and 10 freestanding retail stores.” (CEO Hoff) “Shipments began in the second quarter and are expected to build through the second half of fiscal '27 and into fiscal '28.” (CEO Hoff)

  • Compared with the prior quarter’s framing, management again stressed limited macro recovery while leaning more heavily on tariff recoveries and second-half normalization: “we do not expect meaningful near-term improvement in market conditions.” (CEO Hoff)

Financial Results

  • “Consolidated net sales decreased $6 million, or about 9%, compared to the prior year period, reflecting lower sales across each of our operating segments.” (CFO Earl Armstrong) “Gross margin improved 690 basis points to 31.8%, while operating income improved to $1.3 million compared to an operating loss of $0.5 million in the prior year period.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • “Starting with Hooker Branded, net sales decreased $1.6 million, or 4.5%.” (CFO Armstrong) “Hooker Branded gross profit increased $3.2 million and gross margin improved 1,050 basis points to nearly 40%.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • “Turning now to Domestic Upholstery, net sales decreased $1.5 million, or 5.3%.” (CFO Armstrong) “The segment generated operating income of $833,000 compared with an operating loss of $408,000 in the prior year quarter.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • “Cash and cash equivalents stood at $18.7 million at quarter end, an increase of $8.1 million from the end of the first quarter.” (CFO Armstrong) “Cash generated from operations during the first 6 months was $24 million.” (CFO Armstrong)

Q&A

  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti &u0026 Company, LLC: asked how significant Hooker Branded key SKU out-of-stocks were; CEO Jeremy Hoff: “I can't comment further specifically, but it was definitely a headwind for us… we feel like we started to get through that once we reached July.”

  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti &u0026 Company, LLC: asked for Domestic Upholstery mix between private label/outdoor vs. custom; CFO Earl Armstrong: “We tend to look at it at the segment level, Anthony. And I think that's basically all we can say at this point.” CEO Hoff added: “it's really good business for us, and the category is strong.”

  • Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti &u0026 Company, LLC: asked for Margaritaville revenue and second-half expectations; CEO Jeremy Hoff: “We can't get specific on that, but I will tell you that a big part of it is going to be in the second half.”

  • David Storms, Stonegate Capital Partners: pressed on confidence to reduce promotions in a tough macro; CEO Jeremy Hoff: “High confidence because we already -- we mentioned July… We're confident that that's not going to be a trend moving forward.”

  • David Storms, Stonegate Capital Partners: asked for backlog detail and Margaritaville mix/margins; CEO Jeremy Hoff: “Can't get that specific, but we're encouraged by our backlog, and we feel good about the second half.”

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical on key drivers, pressing for quantification: “How significant was this?” (Anthony Lebiedzinski, Sidoti &u0026 Company, LLC) and “how should we be thinking about maybe your confidence to bring down promotions despite the macro environment?” (David Storms, Stonegate Capital Partners).

  • Management tone was slightly positive in outlook but selective in disclosure: “High confidence…” (CEO Jeremy Hoff) alongside repeated limits such as “We can't get specific on that” (CEO Hoff) and “I think that's basically all we can say at this point.” (CFO Earl Armstrong)

  • Versus last quarter, management leaned more on realized tariff recoveries and near-term operational normalization (promotions, supply flow), while analysts again sought Margaritaville and backlog economics detail.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q2 emphasized tariff recoveries as a central driver: “tariff recoveries significantly and favorably impacted our Q2 results.” (CFO Earl Armstrong) In Q1, the company emphasized cost actions and margins: “we delivered net income of $1.1 million for the quarter, reflecting the benefits of our cost reduction initiatives.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • Q2 added more detail on promotional pressure and channel mix: “a greater mix of e-commerce sales along with targeted promotional activity.” (CEO Jeremy Hoff) Q1 focus included brand/platform changes: “we introduced Hooker Custom Upholstery.” (CEO Hoff)

  • Analyst questioning remained consistent on Margaritaville ramp and backlog, with Q2 continuing to draw “Can't get that specific” responses (CEO Hoff), similar to Q1 tariff-refund uncertainty: “we decided not to disclose that publicly.” (CFO Armstrong)

Risks and Concerns

  • “Housing turnover and big-ticket discretionary demand remain weak, and we do not expect meaningful near-term improvement in market conditions.” (CEO Jeremy Hoff)

  • “higher promotional discounts, and key SKU out-of-stocks due to significantly longer lead times out of Asia” (CFO Earl Armstrong) were cited as near-term headwinds, while management pointed to easing: “Inventory constraints… had largely eased by quarter end.” (CFO Armstrong)

  • The company framed tariff complexity and residual impacts as ongoing context: “The substantial administrative burden these tariffs placed on our team over many months cannot be recovered.” (CEO Hoff)

Final Takeaway

Management attributed Q2 profitability to tariff recoveries and prior fixed-cost reductions while describing a still-weak demand backdrop. For the second half, leadership said promotions should normalize, backlog is up sequentially, and Margaritaville is moving from commitments into shipments, supported by about 100 planned in-store galleries and 10 freestanding stores, while continuing to limit specificity on product-level revenue and margin details.

data.title: Citi initiates short-term upside view on AppLovin, sets $600 target
data.description:
Shares of AppLovin (APP) rose about 2.5% on Friday after Citi said it could gain about 91% over the next 90 days and initiated a short-term upside view on the stock and set a $600 price target.

Analyst Aarushi Gupta said investor disappointment after AppLovin (APP) delivered just 4% sequential topline growth in the second quarter has led some to view the company’s third-quarter guidance of 7% to 8% sequential growth as too aggressive.

The brokerage called that concern "misguided," noting that the second quarter is often the slowest-growth quarter of the year and that the period did not benefit from an Axon model improvement introduced in July.

“As such, we believe AppLovin (APP) is well positioned to meet or exceed its 3Q26 guidance,” Citi said.

Longer term, the analysts expect e-commerce to eventually overtake gaming as the main driver of AppLovin’s (APP) topline growth. They cited e-commerce’s larger total addressable market, attractive return on ad spend from existing clients, and potential acceleration in client onboarding, either organically or through tuck-in acquisitions.

“As confidence in AppLovin’s (APP) growth outlook improves, we see scope for AppLovin’s (APP) multiple to expand,” Citi said.

The brokerage rates the stock buy.

data.title: Oracle's Q1 proves potential of IaaS strategy as cloud infra surges 121%: analysts
data.description:
Oracle's (ORCL) first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings results proved the potential of its infrastructure as a service strategy as cloud infrastructure revenue surged 121% year over year to $7.4B.

Shares initially popped up about 7% during post-market trading on Thursday. However, by noon trading on Friday, shares had increased less than 1%. Despite the lukewarm next-day reaction in the market, analysts across the board were positive on the results.

J.P. Morgan reiterated its Outperform rating and $200 price target.

"The company delivered to expectations with total revenue growth of +30% y/y, tracking above the guide on triple-digit growth in Cloud Infrastructure, and RPO building a further $26B sequentially," said J.P. Morgan analyst Samik Chatterjee in a Friday investor note.

"The strength was evident across multiple drivers: 1) Capacity delivery of 850 MW in the quarter, nearly three times what was delivered in all of F4Q26 and none of it from the flagship sites that have attracted investor scrutiny, which in our view demonstrates the diversification of the build-out and mitigates risk to the medium-term outlook from any single site delay; 2) More than $30B of new AI contracts, primarily booked on prepay or bring-your-own-hardware (BYOH) structures; and 3) Operating leverage and discipline that helped hold PF operating margin flat at ~42% despite the expected step-down in gross margin, reinforcing our view that operating margin, rather than gross margin, is the appropriate lens as infrastructure becomes a larger share of the mix," he added.

Meanwhile, Jefferies reiterated its Buy rating and $290 price target, highlighting Oracle's significant backlog.

"Backlog was $664B (46% y/y growth), up 4% q/q ($26B q/q) vs. 15% in F4Q26 and 6% q/q in F3Q26," said Jefferies analyst Brent Thill in a note. "On a y/y basis, backlog decelerated vs. 363% y/y growth in F4Q. The backlog growth was driven by >$30B of additional AI cloud contracts booked in F1Q. Mgmt indicated that based on the structuring of those new contracts, there is no incremental impact on its plans to raise capital."

Similarly, Citi reiterated its Buy rating and hefty $330 price target.

"Oracle delivered more than 300,000 GPUs during the quarter while adding 850MW of datacenter capacity and older GPUs seeing 20% premium on renewed and resold contracts," Citi analysts said in a note. Roughly half of RPO is expected to flow into revenue over the next 36 months, with RPO conversion to revenue expected to accelerate. Multicloud DB cloud grew 353% y/y, and multicloud customers grew 180% y/y, with multicloud DB regions reaching 70. They also completed their $20B at-the-market equity issuance in Q1."
